quest.title: A Fuel Named "Fate"
quest.description: The threat to Natlan remains unresolved, for the Abyssal tide you shattered was but a reflection emerging from the Night Kingdom. Still more crises await — sorrow, solitude, and death...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x700, Primogem x30, Mora x31125, The Cornerstone of Stars and Flames x1, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x6

talks.objective: Take part in the post-battle banquet

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Everyone, we are gathered here to celebrate a glorious victory.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: It is a victory forged by each and every one of us, and we should all be proud of what we have accomplished.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: We emerge victorious from another crisis to declare: Our beloved Natlan is saved!

dialogues.speaker: Asmerom
dialogues.text: Alright!

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: I must caution that this war is not yet over. We have not destroyed our enemy, merely driven them further into the depths of the Night Kingdom.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: But the Abyss underestimated Natlan's forces, and they have suffered a devastating defeat. It will be a long time before they are able to pose a threat to us again.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: After making some preparations, I will launch my final counterattack. I shall strike them in their lair and wipe them out for good.

dialogues.speaker: Asmerom
dialogues.text: Oh, man...

dialogues.speaker: Berehanu
dialogues.text: Wait, Archon... Are you saying you're going alone?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Yes. The Abyssal energy there is too strong. Contact with it would be instantly lethal to anyone else.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: I'm sure you're all still fired up, and you must be eager to take the fight home to the enemy. But I must ask you to temper your ambitions. I will return victorious, for all of us.

dialogues.speaker: Asmerom
dialogues.text: It's kind of a shame that we can't join in with the final showdown...

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Please, look at the bigger picture. Thanks to every one of you, we have already secured an enormous victory. Tonight, we should celebrate to our hearts' content.

dialogues.speaker: Berehanu
dialogues.text: I guess... if our lives are no longer at risk, things can basically go back to normal, right?

dialogues.speaker: Asmerom
dialogues.text: That's good enough for me. Beats having monsters everywhere.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: When the time comes, I will gather everyone here again.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Now, let us also remember those who gave their lives fighting for our nation.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Once the last dregs of the Abyss are wiped out, I intend to give them the grand funeral they deserve.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: An ancient name could never record the many who we lost, but no hero of Natlan should be forgotten.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: If I may... Let's have a moment of silence for the fallen.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Lastly, there is one more person I must thank for his extraordinary support in our time of need, and that is The Captain.

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: Speaking in a personal capacity, I should like to offer my sincere congratulations on your victory.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Well everyone, please enjoy the victory feast. I hope it's a chance to relax your minds and rekindle your spirits, so that we may face what lies ahead with renewed vigor.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: You did a great job, Kachina. You're much more confident now. Seems like winning the Pilgrimage gave you a real boost.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Hehe, nah, I just figured I should do my part, y'know?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: I spoke to your mom and dad — they were singing your praises. They said the world's your oyster now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How are things at the People of the Springs' base?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: There are some casualties, but the overall mood is very positive. I reckon they'll start rebuilding pretty soon.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Same situation for the Children of Echoes.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Still... it's so sad that some people couldn't be saved by the Ode of Resurrection.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: I think... I wanna hold a candlelight vigil for them when I get home.

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Oh, that's a great idea. Let's do it together.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Let's hope that their sacrifice marks the beginning of a new age for Natlan — an age of unprecedented peace.

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Kinich, you are one lucky devil. I don't know how the heck you're still alive. Pff.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: I'm in a zero-tolerance mood right now. Stop being so flippant.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Unless you want to get punched in the face.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What is it with you, Ajaw? Why are you so incapable of being nice?

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Oh, this is rich! One measly victory, and it's all gone to your head! Hmph, you'd all be mincemeat by now if not for the heroic deeds of the Almighty Dragonlord, K'uhul Ajaw!

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Alright, credit where credit's due. Here's a bunch of grapes for your trouble.

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Don't treat me like I'm your pet parrot!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How are the Scions of the Canopy and the Collective of Plenty?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: The messengers are the worst affected. I expect there'll be delays on all deliveries in Natlan for some time.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Although fortunately, a lot of people have said they're willing to help out part time. That should alleviate the situation.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: The Collective of Plenty was the furthest from the Abyss's entry point, so they didn't have as many monsters to deal with. From what I hear, they got off relatively unscathed.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: But it might have been a different story if Chasca hadn't gotten there when she did...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's good to hear. All's well that ends well.

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Well, whaddya know, these are pretty tasty... Oh, servant! One more bunch of grapes, posthaste!

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Okay, Polly.

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: I must congratulate you on your efforts during this war. I am told you have proven yourself to be an outstanding adventurer and warrior.

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: #You remind me of the {M#Princess}{F#Prince}. The similarities in your approach are striking, especially when you told me you wanted to win.

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: #I hope you will see {M#her}{F#him} soon.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Ororon, how are the Masters of the Night-Wind doing?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Granny Citlali's been there the whole time, and she's a tough one. I think we should be fine...

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: I'm sure there'll be some patching up to do though. That's a job for the young folks — I should probably head back, so I can pitch in.

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: Do you need support from the Fatui?

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: ...Probably not. There are a lot of older folks in our tribe, and I suspect they would find your comrades' presence a little distressing.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Right, 'cause they often look like a bunch of intimidating thugs.

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Well, also, in my tribe, excessive use of elemental energy is bad for your eyesight.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, right... Okay.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: ...Ah. Welcome.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You seem a little out of sorts. Are you just tired, or...?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: I guess I am. You know, when I was up there in the sky, I could see all of Natlan stretching out below me... People everywhere, giving everything they had for a chance at victory.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: I just... If only I'd been quicker, maybe they wouldn't have... And Chuychu, maybe she'd still...

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: ...I'm sorry, now's not the time for that. Um... Fruit juice, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Make it a large...?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: At least it's over now. That's something.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: True. My 500-year plan has almost come to fruition. Just one last step to go.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Namely, my final battle against the Abyss. But battle is second nature to me, so I'm not feeling a huge amount of pressure.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It was so awesome, the way you exploded that thing in the sky with one almighty punch! Are you always gonna have that kind of power from now on?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Oh, that was the divine throne unleashing my full potential, and it was only temporary. I can't wield that power for any length of time — my body wouldn't be able to handle it.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Likewise, the amplified power of the Ode of Resurrection was also temporary. From now on, it's back to ancient name bearers only.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm guessing the Night Warden Wars are over for the foreseeable future?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Correct. We dealt the Abyss a critical blow, so for the time being, it's too weak to sustain regular invasions.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: I hope the people will be able to enjoy this period of peace... Or rather, assuming all goes to plan — eternal peace.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: We've had centuries of war with the Abyss, and it's high time we brought that chapter to a close.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Anyway, there's something I've been wondering about. I know you've been at the center of some major events in other nations too, and fought many powerful foes.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: In this war, you were in the thick of it once again. Dashing around tirelessly, supporting the fighting on all fronts... So tell me, what drives you to do this as a mere Traveler passing through? Why risk life and limb for a cause that's not your own?

choices.text: So I can look back on my journey with a clear conscience.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: A clear conscience... Great answer. That's how life should be lived: to the fullest, with no regrets.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: What I'm really trying to say is... I would love for you, with your extraordinary talent and your sense of justice, to join me in this final step. You and I, together, finally putting an end to the ever-looming threat of the Abyss...

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: But I also don't want to take advantage of your good nature and readiness to help others. The final battle will be very dangerous, and you have the rest of your journey to consider.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: I'm sure you must be weary? Sleep well tonight. Let's talk again tomorrow, in the Speaker's Chamber.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: I'll give you more details on the final battle, and then I hope to hear your verdict.

choices.text: I just can't turn a blind eye to injustice.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: You know, it's that mindset that distinguishes the heroes in every story. They're the natural protagonists.

choices.text: Because Paimon hates to see people suffer.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...What's this got to do with Paimon?

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: #Hahaha, {M#he's just showing how much you mean to him, in his own way.}{F#she's just showing how much you mean to her, in her own way.}

Go to the Speaker's Chamber to look for Mavuika

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: #Hey, {NICKNAME}, Paimon. There you are, I've been looking all over for you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, hey Citlali. What's up?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Listen up. I have something really important to tell you...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Citlali quickly explains her concerns about Mavuika's death.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What? Are you serious?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So Mavuika still has to die...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Natlan must pay the price for Mavuika's use of the Ruler of Death's power. That price is death, and only Mavuika's death can clear the debt.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I had thought that the Ruler of Death might have a change of heart after seeing the people of Natlan come together and fight so bravely. But...

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Even now that the war's over and the threat to Natlan is gone, it looks like that death is still set in stone.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I had to know your thoughts — I want to save her, but I can't do it alone.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'll see what I can do.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Okay, good. That makes me feel a little better.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Thank you for standing up for us. There's clearly something special about you, so if anyone has a chance of defying the rules, that would be you.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Oh, and please don't breathe a word of this to Mavuika.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: I'm sure she's well aware of the cost of using the divine throne's power. But if she finds out that anyone else knows, it could ruin our chances to help.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Got it. Mum's the word.

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Alright, that was the last major item on my to-do list. Now, since I've come all this way, I think it's finally time for a well-earned drink.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... G—Go easy though, yeah?

dialogues.speaker: Citlali
dialogues.text: Don't worry, I said "a" drink. That means just one.

dialogues.speaker: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night
dialogues.text: The outlander with deep ties to this land returns... and this time, he is alone?

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: The power that the Pyro Archon used to strike back at the Abyss came from the Ruler of Death. From what I know of her rules, she will demand death in return.

dialogues.speaker: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night
dialogues.text: How do you know of this?

dialogues.speaker: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night
dialogues.text: ...I see. So, the Ruler of Death sent you on your long journey.

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: Natlan still has a final battle to fight, and I too have a final foe to face.

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: For the sake of those countless lost souls, and a hope for Natlan's future... I need your help.

dialogues.speaker: Sundjatta
dialogues.text: Alright, you little munchkin! If you keep pestering me, I'm gonna have to get serious.

dialogues.speaker: Sundjatta
dialogues.text: I get a hundred kids a day telling me they want to be the next Pyro Archon. So, why should I train you?

dialogues.speaker: Sundjatta
dialogues.text: *sigh* Nagging isn't going to accomplish anything. No one can predict the future, and unless you have some exceptional, jaw-dropping talent I'm unaware of—

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: "I can shoot those cornflakes in your kitchen from right here."

dialogues.speaker: Sundjatta
dialogues.text: Hahaha, don't be ridiculous! You couldn't make that shot from all the way over here. ...Wait, hold on, you could hurt someone with that...

dialogues.speaker: Sundjatta
dialogues.text: ...Well I'll be. You made the shot.

dialogues.speaker: Sundjatta
dialogues.text: The Scions of the Canopy raise 'em tough... That's some real skill you've got there, little lady. Maybe you really will be Pyro Archon one day.

dialogues.speaker: Burkina
dialogues.text: See this? I'm the first one of us to get an ancient name — and not just any ancient name, but Mal{RUBY#[D]Turnfire}ipo!

dialogues.speaker: Burkina
dialogues.text: If you ask me nicely, there's still time to join my team for the Pilgrimage, y'know...

dialogues.speaker: Burkina
dialogues.text: No need to scowl... You lost, and I won, it's no big deal. You want me to be happy for you when your turn comes, right? So cheer up.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: "I'll get my own ancient name soon enough. And it'll be an even better one than yours."

dialogues.speaker: Burkina
dialogues.text: Oh really? Well, good luck with that... What ancient name could beat Mal{RUBY#[D]Turnfire}ipo in our tribe?

dialogues.speaker: Burkina
dialogues.text: Unless... Surely you don't mean Kion{RUBY#[D]Leader}gozi?

dialogues.speaker: Wanjiru
dialogues.text: Ah, that was fantastic! I can't believe I beat you in a wrestling match for once.

dialogues.speaker: Wanjiru
dialogues.text: Can't be more than a few days now until you're officially made the Pyro Archon. Heh, imagine me trying to schedule a wrestling session with you after that...

dialogues.speaker: Wanjiru
dialogues.text: "Excuse me, Pyro Archon, but would you be able to take a day off from running the nation to wrestle with me?" Hahaha.

dialogues.speaker: Wanjiru
dialogues.text: I heard that the Pyro Archon inherits the knowledge stored in the Sacred Flame, and apparently, it can change your personality... I can't help but feel a little worried.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: "Worried that you won't be able to beat me in a wrestling match anymore?"

dialogues.speaker: Wanjiru
dialogues.text: Why would I be worried about that!? Ugh, never mind, clearly I'm just overthinking things. Why would you forget about me just because of some new job? Even if that job happens to be archon.

dialogues.speaker: Wanjiru
dialogues.text: Come on, one more round!

dialogues.speaker: Ronova
dialogues.text: The victors shall burn bright, while the losers must turn to ash...

dialogues.speaker: Ronova
dialogues.text: I have done what is required of me. The rules are now written into the Night Kingdom, and this will help you to stand against the Abyss.

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: It is still not enough.

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: All this can do is give my people courage. It will not see us through a true catastrophe.

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: If you are to make the Natlanese alone bear the consequences of a broken world, you will have to bring more to the bargaining table.

dialogues.speaker: Ronova
dialogues.text: ...You are the greediest human I have ever met, and the fiercest negotiator. No other would seriously ask to borrow my power.

dialogues.speaker: Ronova
dialogues.text: My domain is death, and its power comes at a great price... The question is, are you prepared to pay?

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: I need that power. Only a hero can truly wield it, and heroes are not afraid of dying.

dialogues.speaker: Ronova
dialogues.text: No, a fear of death is ingrained in all living things. If the wielder of this power cannot conquer their fear, countless innocent lives will be claimed in their stead, for only then can the price be paid.

dialogues.speaker: Ronova
dialogues.text: Those are the rules.

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: Mine is a nation that will not yield to the Abyss. It will certainly not yield to your rules.

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: As their culture and civilization is transmitted through the generations, and their faith grows, the people will go from strength to strength, and reach heights that even I cannot dream of.

dialogues.speaker: Ronova
dialogues.text: Very well. I shall agree to help you. But I am merely a Shade, and I do not have as much freedom to do as I please as you might think.

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: Then what do you propose?

dialogues.speaker: Ronova
dialogues.text: Keep this a secret.

dialogues.speaker: Ronova
dialogues.text: If I am questioned about it, I will deny all involvement, and claim: "That treacherous Xbalanque stole my power."

dialogues.speaker: Xbalanque
dialogues.text: That will not be a problem. Thank you, I am glad we could reach an agreement.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Come in.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: As you know, I've asked you to come here to discuss the task of wiping out the Abyss.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Oh, but first — any progress on the Ancient Name?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I've received the gift from the Lord of the Night.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: I'm surprised she was willing to help you... and, by extension, me. I'm very grateful to her.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Wait, hold on, wasn't the whole point of the Ancient Names for winning that huge battle? Why would {NICKNAME} still need one by this point?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Because she wants me to join her in the final battle.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: That's right. The Abyss has retreated to the depths of the Night Kingdom, a place that has long since been corrupted by Abyssal energy...

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: If we don't finish them off and restore the Ley Lines, the threat they pose to Natlan will remain. The battle we fought yesterday, we may one day have to fight again.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: This is the fate Natlan has always been resigned to. For thousands of years, we have struggled on the brink of a looming darkness, and never known true peace.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: But this time, I want to break the cycle and free us from this fate for good.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: With the sacred flame, I can protect myself from the Abyssal corruption, but beyond that, you are the only other person who can resist it.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: If your ancient name can't be forged, I will go alone. But if it can, I'd really love your help.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is the Ode of Resurrection working again?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Not completely — after all, the Night Kingdom is still plagued by Abyssal corruption.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: But when I used the power of the divine throne, it dispelled a lot of that corruption. Plus, your ancient name is a special case, so the Lord of the Night will take special care of you.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: In short, the Ode of Resurrection still has a number of limitations, but I can promise that it will work reliably on you.

choices.text: Good. Then I will join you in battle.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa whoa whoa, aren't we forgetting something here? What about Paimon? What's her place in all this?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What!? You mean, we'll be separated?

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: The Abyss is extremely devious. If you two go there together, you can bet they'll make Paimon their primary target just to put us in an impossible position.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon wasn't that worried, but... now she's petrified...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What will you do without me!?

choices.text: I'll be a complete mess, I'm sure.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, well... Paimon needs to think about this, because you're really asking a lot of her. But give Paimon some time, and she'll do her best to rise to the challenge...

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: Everyone in Natlan knows how important this final battle is. You will be remembered and revered long into the future, until the end of time.

response.speaker: Mavuika
response.text: If you have any other questions, please ask away.

choices.text: But only for a short time.
Sounds like I'm your only option anyway.

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: If you're making candles, I have some materials you can use. They're in the warehouse. Should have plenty to spare.

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Oh, okay! Um, I guess I'll... tread carefully on the way in, then? Or...

dialogues.speaker: Xilonen
dialogues.text: Oh, good point. I'll go instead.

dialogues.speaker: Iansan
dialogues.text: Everyone else is enjoying the celebration, but Ajaw's still being as aggravating as ever. Does he have a chip on his shoulder? What's it about?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: In fairness, repeating a few set phrases ad nauseum is all parrots know how to do.

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: I am NOT a parrot! I am the Almighty Dragonlord, K'uhul Ajaw!

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: I am still somewhat in disbelief that a united people prevailed against the Abyss...

dialogues.speaker: Ororon
dialogues.text: Do I sense some regret in your words?

dialogues.speaker: "The Captain"
dialogues.text: A degree of regret is inevitable. But above all, I feel profound admiration.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: My mind is still flooded with scenes from the war. I can't get the images out of my head...

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Maybe I need another drink.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Mavuika said she had more to discuss with us today. Let's head to the Speaker's Chamber.
